page: Microsoft Azure E96-24ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with a constrained vCPU count to serve memory-intensive workloads. It is powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance provides 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX).

Memory capacity is configured at 768.0 GB, yielding an allocation of 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Benchmark data shows strong uncached memory bandwidth, reaching 190.74 GB/sec for read operations and 120.18 GB/sec for write operations on 256 MB test blocks. In single-core compute tasks, Geekbench scored 2,156.0, showing strong single-thread capability alongside strong image processing (15,402.0) and text processing (2,679.0) scores. Multi-core performance aligns with the 24-vCPU allocation, recording a stress-ng multi-core score of 23,970.13 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 15,275.0.

Storage consists of 5,669 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD capacity, providing fast scratch space and direct I/O throughput. The instance includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses and contains no discrete graphics hardware. In real-world data handling, it achieves 33.51 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and sustained throughput in small-model text generation at 286.32 tokens per second.

The constrained vCPU design offers cost efficiency for applications licensed on a per-core basis that simultaneously require substantial memory pools and fast NVMe scratch storage. Primary workload targets include large in-memory databases such as Redis, enterprise relational database systems, and heavy ETL or analytics pipelines.

Designed for core-licensed, memory-heavy applications, the instance provides 768.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 32.0 GB per core ratio, along with 5,669 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. It supports advanced vector and matrix instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX. Benchmark results highlight strong uncached memory bandwidth reaching 190.74 GB/sec read and 120.18 GB/sec write throughput, accompanied by strong Geekbench single-core and text processing scores. The instance lacks discrete GPUs and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. It is designed for in-memory databases, large-scale caching systems such as Redis, enterprise relational databases, and data-intensive batch analytics.
